column7: R3 (b): the single-head simplification occurrence: the head match compiled from the head pattern, the guard inline, the cut, the removal of self, the body; a CHR constraint posted inside a guard runs as the oracle runs it

R3 (c): multi-head rules: one loop predicate per occurrence and partner over the partner's store, read through a shared variable's suspension list (newvia) else the global list; a kept self is re-activated and the loop continues, a removed self stops it; the firing order is the store order, newest first

R3 (d): a propagation occurrence keeps every head; the propagation history (novel_production, extend_history on the rule's id tuple) stops a re-firing; a single-head propagation rule fires once per constraint; the second witness is cut with chr_option(debug, off): late storage lists hailstone(27) first where the eager order of cc04_prop lists hailstone(1) first (ARCH-PROLOG-CLPR-CHR section 8)

R4: a constraint on an unbound variable is re-run by attr_unify_hook when the variable is bound or unified with another attributed variable (the v(Mask, L1..Lk) merge, then run_suspensions per constraint in declaration order)

R7: find_chr_constraint/1, current_chr_constraint/1 and chr_show_store/1 enumerate through the generated enumerate rows in declaration order, each store newest first; chr_show_store prints one constraint per line as the vendored runtime prints it
R6: the pass runs inside a module section; the continuation goal and the attribute module carry the module's name; the generated clauses stay in the module

R8: the standard order of two unbound variables is their creation order, carried by a creation serial in the unbound cell (the collector relocates cells, so an address is no order); a clause's fresh variables are created at their first textual occurrence, left to right, never inner-first by the term builder; dump/3 then solves for the variable swipl solves for
